reference_site_analysis.summary: A single-page, vertically-scrolling Valentine proposal site with three full-viewport sections, a deep burgundy color palette, floating heart particles, and two key playful mechanics.
page_flow: Section 1 — The Ask: Full-screen hero with large serif heading, subtitle, Yes/No buttons
Section 2 — Our Memories: Photo carousel with romantic images, auto-play, dot navigation
Section 3 — My Love For You: Word-by-word animated love letter that builds on scroll

core_interactions.dodging_no_button: On hover, the No button jumps to a random screen position. It persists across all sections at z-index 9999, always visible but effectively uncatchable.
core_interactions.growing_yes_button: When No is hovered, the Yes button grows larger, centers itself, and gains sparkle effects — making it the obvious and only real choice.
core_interactions.celebration_modal: Clicking Yes triggers a centered modal with animated pulsing heart, 'Yayyyy' headline, 'I knew it!' subtext, sparkle decorations, and blurred background.
core_interactions.photo_carousel: Auto-sliding image carousel with 5 images, dot indicators, and pause/play toggle.
core_interactions.word_reveal: Love letter text animates word-by-word via individually wrapped spans, likely triggered by scroll/intersection observer.

reference_site_analysis.emotional_tone: Warm, playful, romantic. The dodging button creates laughter. The love letter creates intimacy. The celebration creates shared joy.

design_language.colors: Deep burgundy background, coral/salmon red accents, soft pink, cream highlights
design_language.typography: Large serif for headings (white + coral accent words), sans-serif for body, italic for emotional subtexts
design_language.atmosphere: Candlelit, intimate. Floating semi-transparent heart particles across all sections.

essential: Full-screen 'Will you be my Valentine?' hero section
Yes/No buttons with the dodging No mechanic
Celebration state when Yes is clicked
skip: Share/Send to Loved One button (adds complexity, not needed for private use)
Dot navigation for carousel (swipe is sufficient on mobile)

copy: Replace generic subtitle with something personal — an inside joke or shared reference
Write the love letter in your own voice, not the generic template
Personalize the celebration modal text (e.g., reference tonight's dinner)
visuals: Replace stock photos with real photos of the two of you
Add a personal detail to the color scheme if she has a favorite color
interactions: The No button could show escalating funny messages each time it dodges (e.g., 'Nice try', 'Not happening', 'I said NO to No')
Celebration modal could include a specific call-to-action for tonight (e.g., 'See you at dinner')
The Yes button could show a heart icon that pulses on hover

prd.overview: A single-page, mobile-first webpage that asks the user's girlfriend to be his Valentine. The page uses playful interaction design (a dodging No button) to create laughter, a personal love letter to create intimacy, and a celebration state to create shared joy. It will be shown tonight at dinner.
prd.target_user: One specific person — the builder's girlfriend, viewing on her phone at dinner.
prd.user_goal: She taps the link, smiles or laughs at the playful interaction, feels loved by the personal content, and taps Yes.
success_criteria: Page loads in under 2 seconds on mobile
The No button is clearly uncatchable on both desktop and mobile (touch and hover)
Clicking Yes produces a satisfying, visible celebration
All personal copy feels genuine, not like a template
Page is fully usable on an iPhone screen without horizontal scrolling
Can be deployed to a public URL (Vercel, Netlify, or similar) within the build session

core_features.name: Hero Section — The Ask
core_features.description: Full-viewport section with centered heading 'Will you be my Valentine?', a personal subtitle, and Yes/No buttons. Deep burgundy-to-dark gradient background.
acceptance: Heading is large, readable, uses serif font with accent color on 'Valentine'
Subtitle is personal and italicized
Yes button is prominent with heart icon and gradient fill
No button is outlined/secondary style
Section fills exactly one viewport height

core_features.name: Dodging No Button
core_features.description: The No button repositions to a random location on screen when the user hovers (desktop) or taps (mobile). It should be amusing, not frustrating.
acceptance: On desktop: repositions on mouseenter/hover
On mobile: repositions on touchstart
Never repositions off-screen — always visible but unreachable
Yes button grows slightly and optionally sparkles when No is dodged
Button persists and continues dodging if user scrolls to other sections

core_features.name: Celebration State
core_features.description: Modal or full-screen takeover triggered by clicking Yes. Shows animated heart, celebratory text, and personal message.
acceptance: Pulsing/bouncing heart animation
Celebratory headline (personalized, not generic)
Background blurs or dims
Optional: confetti or sparkle particle effect
Includes a warm personal closing line referencing tonight

core_features.name: Floating Hearts Background
core_features.description: Semi-transparent heart shapes floating gently across the viewport as ambient decoration.
acceptance: Hearts are CSS-only or lightweight SVG — no heavy libraries
Varying sizes and opacities
Smooth float animation (not janky on mobile)
Fixed position so they persist across scroll

core_features.name: Personal Photo Carousel
core_features.description: Section 2: 'Our Memories' — a horizontal carousel of personal photos with captions.
acceptance: Auto-advances every 4-5 seconds
Manual swipe on mobile, click navigation optional on desktop
Rounded corners, subtle shadow on images
Placeholder images acceptable for initial build, replaced with real photos before deploy

core_features.name: Love Letter Section
core_features.description: Section 3: A personal love letter with word-by-word or line-by-line reveal animation triggered on scroll.
acceptance: Text appears progressively as user scrolls into view
Uses Intersection Observer for scroll-triggered animation
Serif or handwriting-style font for the letter body
Decorative heart elements above and below

non_goals: No backend, database, or server-side logic
No CMS or content editing UI
Not a reusable template — this is a one-time personal page
ux_flow: 1. She receives a link (texted or shown at dinner) and opens it on her phone
2. Page loads instantly — she sees the hero: 'Will you be my Valentine?' with a personal subtitle
3. Floating hearts drift gently in the background
4. She notices Yes and No buttons
5. She taps No (if she tries) — it jumps away, she laughs. Yes button grows. Repeat as many times as she wants.
7. Celebration modal appears — animated heart, joyful text, personal message about tonight's dinner
8. She scrolls down (or celebration auto-dismisses) to see the memories carousel with your photos
9. She scrolls further to read the love letter, words appearing one by one
10. Page ends with decorative hearts and a warm closing

content_and_tone_guidelines.voice: First-person, intimate, slightly playful. Write like you're talking to her, not like a greeting card.
content_and_tone_guidelines.headline: Keep 'Will you be my Valentine?' — it is the classic, and it works.
content_and_tone_guidelines.subtitle: Replace the generic 'I've been waiting to ask you this...' with something personal. Example: a reference to your first date, an inside joke, or a specific compliment.
content_and_tone_guidelines.celebration_text: Should feel like genuine excitement, not performative. Reference tonight's dinner specifically.
content_and_tone_guidelines.love_letter: Write this yourself. 4-6 sentences. Mention specific memories, things you love about her, and why she matters to you. The word-by-word animation will give each word weight — shorter is better.
things_to_avoid: Generic greeting card language ('You complete me', 'You're the sunshine in my life')
Anything that reads like it was written by AI
Overly long text — the animations need breathing room

technical_constraints.stack: Next.js 15 (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind CSS. All interactive components use 'use client' directive.
technical_constraints.alternative_stack: Original option was single HTML + Tailwind CDN, but Next.js chosen for native Vercel deployment, next/image optimization, and next/font self-hosting.
technical_constraints.deployment: Vercel — native Next.js deployment. Static export via `output: 'export'` in next.config.ts.
technical_constraints.performance: No heavy dependencies. Total page weight under 500KB excluding photos. CSS animations over JS animations where possible. next/image for automatic WebP conversion and lazy loading. next/font for zero layout shift.
technical_constraints.compatibility: Must work on Safari iOS (her phone, most likely) and Chrome. Test touch events.
technical_constraints.fonts: Self-hosted via next/font — Playfair Display (serif) and Inter (sans-serif). No external CDN requests.
technical_constraints.images: Optimized via next/image — automatic WebP conversion, responsive sizing, lazy loading. Real photos placed in public/photos/.

open_questions: What personal photos should go in the carousel? (Need 3-5 photos ready before deploy)
What is the personal subtitle for the hero? (Inside joke, first date reference, etc.)
What should the love letter say? (Builder should draft this — it must be authentic)
What is the celebration message referencing tonight? (e.g., 'Can't wait for dinner tonight' or 'See you at [restaurant name]')
Does she have a favorite color that should influence the palette, or is the burgundy/pink/coral scheme good?
Should the No button show escalating funny messages, or just silently dodge?
assumptions: She will view this on an iPhone (mobile-first is critical)
She has not seen the reference site (the interaction will feel fresh)
The link will be shared at or just before dinner tonight
Photos are available and can be added before deployment
The builder will write the personal copy (love letter, subtitle, celebration text) — the PRD provides structure, not final words
Vercel or Netlify account is available for deployment
